directAnswer: Pope Innocent VII was Cosimo de' Migliorati of Sulmona, elected in Rome on 17 October 1404 during the Western Schism; he reigned until his death on 6 November 1406. His two years were troubled by unrest in Rome, and he made little progress toward ending the schism, though he planned the revival of the Roman university with the study of Greek.

sections.h2: Cosimo de' Migliorati, Jurist and Collector
paras: Cosimo de' Migliorati was born at Sulmona in the Abruzzo, then part of the Kingdom of Naples. He studied and taught law, served the curia for years, including in England as a papal collector, and became archbishop of Ravenna and bishop of Bologna. Urban VI made him a cardinal in 1389.
When Boniface IX died, the cardinals of the Roman obedience each swore that, if elected, they would work to end the schism, even by resigning. They chose Cosimo, an elderly man of good reputation.

Roman factions, encouraged by King Ladislaus of Naples, contested papal authority in the city. In 1405 the pope's nephew Ludovico Migliorati had a group of Roman representatives seized and killed, provoking an uprising that forced Innocent to flee to Viterbo. He returned in 1406 after the Romans submitted to him again.

Innocent planned to restore the University of Rome and to establish teaching in Greek, and the humanist Leonardo Bruni served in his chancery. The schism remained unresolved. He died in Rome on 6 November 1406 and was buried in St. Peter's.

keyFacts: Born Cosimo de' Migliorati at Sulmona, Kingdom of Naples
Canon lawyer; archbishop of Ravenna and bishop of Bologna
Elected 17 October 1404 after swearing to work for the end of the schism
Driven from Rome to Viterbo in 1405 after violence by his nephew

faqs.question: Why did Innocent VII flee Rome?
faqs.answer: In 1405 his nephew Ludovico Migliorati had several Roman representatives killed, sparking a revolt that forced the pope to withdraw to Viterbo. He returned the next year.

faqs.question: Did Innocent VII try to end the Western Schism?
faqs.answer: He had sworn to work for unity, but his short and troubled reign brought no real progress. The schism was ended only at the Council of Constance.
